findings.title: Exit-code contract changed: 4 no longer means "recreate required"
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` result. These constants are the documented, scriptable contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` (the guide explicitly tells users to rely only on the exit code). Any existing consumer that hardcodes 4 as "recreate upgrade needed" – including automation pipelines and any operator/job code that inspects the terminated container's exit code – will now silently interpret "the rolling-updates feature is disabled" as "perform a recreate upgrade", and will no longer recognise a real recreate result (3). No non-documentation consumer was updated in this PR; please confirm every reader of these codes uses the constants, and consider picking an unused code (e.g. 5) for the new condition instead of recycling 4.

findings.title: Documented update-compatibility command appends --features, overriding the user's feature set
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders every command in the Update Compatibility guide as `bin/kc.sh update-compatibility <sub> ... --features=rolling-updates`. `--features` is a single, replacing list, not additive, so a user who copies this command loses all other features they have configured (via `KC_FEATURES`, keycloak.conf or the image build). Since the guide simultaneously warns that "omitting any configuration options will result in incomplete metadata", the documented command produces metadata for a different feature set than the running deployment. In addition, `features` is a build-time option, so for an optimized distribution/image passing it on the CLI is rejected or forces re-augmentation. The guide should instruct users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list (or enable it at build time) rather than show a bare `--features=rolling-updates`.

findings.title: New FEATURE_DISABLED exit code is not covered by tests
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and only for the `metadata` subcommand. The newly introduced exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), which is now part of the documented contract and which also collides with the previous meaning of exit code 4 (recreate upgrade), is never asserted; neither is the feature-disabled path of the `check` subcommand. Also no test asserts the new recreate exit code 3. A future renumbering or a regression in the feature gate would not be caught. Add assertions on `exitCode()` for both subcommands with the feature disabled, and for the recreate result.

findings.title: Operator CAUTION about required feature is overbroad/ambiguous
findings.body: The new CAUTION states unconditionally that "the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." That contradicts the behaviour exercised by `UpgradeTest`, which enables the feature only when `spec.update.strategy` is set and still runs successfully (default/unset strategy) without the feature. As written, readers will think the feature is mandatory for every Keycloak CR managed by the Operator. The text should state precisely when the feature is required (e.g. only when `spec.update` is used) and what "fail" means (CR in error status, reconciliation error).

findings.title: Test replaces instead of appending the CR's enabled features
findings.body: `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` unconditionally overwrites whatever `spec.features.enabled` the base test deployment provides. If the shared test CR template ever enables another feature, it is silently dropped here and the test would exercise a different configuration than intended (or fail for an unrelated reason). The existing list should be read and extended with `rolling-updates`.
